subject: Follow-up: Billing correction and evidence for duplicated token counts during Mar 1 incident
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Jenna Park <jenna@logiserve.com>
Cc: billing@logiserve.com
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Incident: Billing anomaly affecting LogiServe — preliminary notice

Hi Jenna,

I wanted to let you know about a billing anomaly we detected this morning that impacted a small subset of customer request streams, including LogiServe. Our telemetry shows a short-lived duplicate token accounting event between 08:45 and 09:05 PST on 2027-03-01.

What we're doing now:
- We’ve paused the affected aggregation pipeline and deployed a fix.
- Engineering is performing a token-level recount for all invoices touched during the window.
- We will proactively issue a credit for any confirmed duplicated tokens; we expect to have a preliminary recount and proposed credit by EOD tomorrow (Mar 2).

Immediate ask: can you confirm the invoice number you’d like us to apply any credit to? You can reply to billing@logiserve.com and I’ll make sure the team ties the credit to your account.

I’m sorry for the disruption — we know this is sensitive for billing. I’ll keep you updated with the recount and the artifact (CSV) that shows the before/after counts.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Account Manager, Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0172

Also please send the timeframe and any ticket number you have for this incident so we can track internally.

Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 15:30:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Incident: Billing anomaly affecting LogiServe — recount results and credit applied (INV-20270227)

Hi Jenna,

Thank you for your patience. We completed the token recount for the requested invoice window and attached the artifacts below. Summary:

- Affected window: 2027-03-01 08:45:00 PST through 2027-03-01 09:05:00 PST.
- Root cause (short): an aggregation duplication bug in a metrics pipeline caused a subset of generation requests to be counted twice in billing telemetry for certain request IDs. Embeddings telemetry was not affected.
- Impact for LogiServe (INV-20270227): 9,412 duplicated generation tokens were billed originally; corrected count removes the duplication resulting in a net refund of $283.56.
- Action taken: we have applied a credit of $283.56 to invoice INV-20270227 and issued Credit Note: CN-LS-2027-009. You should see the credit reflected in your billing portal within one business day.

Attached artifacts:
- usage_recount-LogiServe-20270301.csv (request-level before/after counts and deltas)
- credit_note-LS-2027-042.pdf (formal credit note: CN-LS-2027-009)

Technical notes (for your ops team):
- The duplication occurred only in the generation (text completion) path; embeddings and reranking streams are unaffected.
- The duplication originated from a retry-aggregation edge case when the KV-cache warmup coincided with a metrics flush. Engineering has patched the metric aggregation code and added an additional validation step to the billing pipeline.

Ticket and postmortem: Redwood ticket #5421 is open for this incident and we have published an internal postmortem here: https://redwood.app/internal/postmortems/INC-20270301. We will publish a customer-readable postmortem summary to our status page by EOD Mar 4.

Please let me know if you need the credit applied differently (refund via ACH or rebate to next invoice). If everything looks good, I'll mark the ticket resolved from our side.

Best regards,
Olga Petrov
Account Manager, Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.com
